# Professional CAD feature matrix

<!-- Generated by scripts/cad-matrix.mjs. Edit cad-feature-matrix.json, then run pnpm cad:matrix. -->

Updated 2026-10-12; repository baseline `b0b5d4f`.

**339 feature contracts · 27 areas · 26 Done · 313 Not done.** These are inventory counts, not a percentage of professional CAD parity.

Union of professional drafting, mechanical/product design and specialist CAD workflows. Product/edition entitlements are not asserted; specialist rows remain visible and count as Not done until delivered. This is a maintained inventory, not a claim that every vendor command or future capability has been enumerated.

## Binary completion contract

The done boolean is the only completion field. A row is Done only when its entire acceptance contract has passing end-to-end evidence. Existing code, unsupported scope, missing proof and failed budgets all remain Not done.

For authoring features, verify real controls (or explicitly named public API), accurate geometry/units, a useful rejection, Undo/Redo where applicable and native persistence. Source and geometry authority remain shared. Format-fidelity contracts additionally require declared format versions and independent-tool fidelity checks. Navigation/read-only rows need their stated visible result without a fictitious persistence requirement.

Done is bounded by the written row scope. Keep its executable journey and dated result. Historical evidence is identified; a known regression immediately resets done to false. No partial, planned or in-progress completion state and no percentage score.

A foundation link identifies code worth reusing; it is not completion evidence. A catalog link establishes coverage context, not a claim that every listed product or subscription implements every row. Acceptance criteria are Partbench's proposed requirements.

## How to hill climb

Fix regressions in Done rows first. Within the ordered frontier, choose a dependency-ready row that unlocks a complete user deliverable; extend its nearest E2E journey. Do not split easy rows or delete hard rows to inflate completion counts.

1. Run `pnpm cad:matrix --next` to inspect the ordered frontier and unmet prerequisites. Priority 0 is responsiveness; 1 is drawing/exchange foundations; 2 is daily-use mechanical/platform work; 3 is broader product design; 4 is specialist workflows. Priority is ordering, never completion status.
2. Take the first useful dependency-ready contract, retain its full scope and implement through the shared document/geometry authority. Prefer a prerequisite that unlocks several complete user workflows. Performance measurements do not flip a row until its whole budget passes.
3. Extend the nearest real browser or public MCP journey. Prove its success, applicable persistence/history, and a rejected operation. Reuse setup; add no unit tests or one-test-per-row suite.
4. Record the command, source revision, date, result and limitations; link that evidence and set `done: true` only after the complete contract passes. A known regression sets it back to `false`.
5. Run `pnpm cad:matrix` to regenerate this table and `pnpm verify` before landing. The matrix check validates links, binary states, evidence references, prerequisites, cycles and generated-document freshness; it cannot establish that a capability works.

Keep IDs stable. Add newly discovered gaps; do not hide specialist rows, weaken budgets or subdivide already-passing rows to improve the count. Changes to acceptance scope require an explicit rationale and fresh applicable evidence. Listing a future capability does not authorize new services, licenses or architecture by itself.

## Current implementation frontier

Cold import remains first. `PERF-003` is the implementation approach to `PERF-001`, not a substitute for its usable-view budget. Native read/transfer alone previously exceeded that budget; optimize that stage as well as staging later work. Define the repeatable corpus in `PERF-012` alongside it. Then establish drawing semantics and DWG feasibility before spending effort on isolated drafting tools.

<a id="evidence-progressiveImport"></a>

### progressiveImport

2026-10-12; source: 2dddce8 (integrated check); five-run implementation base ffb2ebc. Five consecutive fresh-browser production runs: visible native orbit by 4.11–8.77 s, correctly placed progressive geometry before checkpoints finish, camera continuity, atomic source, native payload parity, active-worker Cancel preserving prior document and view, invalid STEP rejection. Full 20-stage engine workflow and pnpm verify pass. Exact editing readiness remains 69.62–89.23 s; no PERF-002 or hardware frame-budget claim. After DRAW-001 integration, the expanded full suite, 20-stage headless workflow and another production browser journey pass; orbit is verified at 6.31 s.

Command: `pnpm smoke:engine-interchange; pnpm --filter @web-cad/web build; five isolated invocations of PARTBENCH_SMOKE_UI_PRODUCTION=1 pnpm smoke:engine-interchange:browser`.

Journeys: [examples/editable-interchange/engine-browser-use.json](../examples/editable-interchange/engine-browser-use.json), [scripts/smoke-editable-interchange.mjs](../scripts/smoke-editable-interchange.mjs).

Recorded results: [docs/import-performance.md](../docs/import-performance.md), [examples/editable-interchange/progressive-import-evidence.json](../examples/editable-interchange/progressive-import-evidence.json), [examples/editable-interchange/engine-evidence.json](../examples/editable-interchange/engine-evidence.json).
